title: VRGDG SeedVR2 TensorRT Studio adds a local Windows workflow around SeedVR2
summary: The public Studio repository packages local preview, comparison, TensorRT VAE decoding and resumable long-video rendering around a compatible SeedVR2 integration. Its GitHub Releases page has no releases, multi-file batch processing is not verified, and early public issues include setup OOM and a reported chunk-assembly failure.
research_notes:
Use the repository installer on Windows 11 with a current NVIDIA RTX driver and at least 35 GB free space. It builds TensorRT engines locally for that GPU and runtime; do not copy plan files across GPU models or TensorRT versions.

Load one source video, choose the render target, set a short preview range, and inspect Original, Restored, Compare (the draggable wipe), or Side by side before the full render. The creator documentation also tells users to confirm faces, freckles, moles, and other permanent marks in the preview.

For a long single video, the creator documentation says resumable rendering can choose a chunk length automatically or manually from 30 seconds to 30 minutes and retry from the first unfinished chunk. Our delivery caution is to inspect the completed file's duration, audio duration, joins, and full decode: Issue #30 reports two playable chunks but a faulty assembled video.

Keep TensorRT engine creation part of the machine-specific setup. The installer provides an exporter and builder, not portable engine files; resume a stopped setup rather than moving another machine's plans.

Use the per-job folder under outputs to keep rendered media, manifests, and logs together, then reopen a selected output from the current workspace when needed.

Use the documented TensorRT temporal-batch choices, 5 or 21, as application options rather than a generic SeedVR2 range. The current source does not support a universal batch-size recommendation.

Do not describe a temporal batch as multi-file batch processing. The issue list showed a 2026-09-02 open request for multiple files one after another; no completed multi-file queue evidence was found.

If TensorRT decoding fails after restoration, the documented path retries saved latents through the internal Stable decoder. Treat that as a fallback with different speed characteristics, then inspect the output rather than assuming an identical accelerated result.

Treat the creator's approximately eight-minute RTX 5090 example as a single reported run: 8 seconds of 360p source to 2K using 7B Sharp FP16. It lacks enough runtime and media detail to estimate throughput or select hardware.

Keep optional extra filters conservative and inspect a preview. A Reddit commenter said that adding extra filters made their result flickery; this is one community report, not a confirmed cause or general preset.
